**Symptom Relief and Treatment Continuation**

Symptom relief was reported in 26 of 30 patients with available symptom data (86.7%). Anticancer treatment continued without interruption in 24 of 33 patients (72.7%). These denominators differ because not all patients had symptom data recorded.

**What the Results Support**

The series supports feasibility: high-dose oral vitamin D was administered alongside ongoing anticancer therapy without reported treatment-related adverse events, and most patients maintained their cancer treatment schedule. The observed symptom relief in the majority of those assessed is encouraging as a signal warranting further study.

**Limits of Causal and Safety Claims**

Causation cannot be inferred. Thirty of 33 patients received concurrent supportive therapy, and no untreated or placebo-controlled comparator existed, so improvement cannot be attributed to vitamin D alone. The 10-day observation window and inconsistent post-treatment laboratory data (vitamin D levels measured in only 13 patients) preclude conclusions about general safety. Without documented calcium monitoring, renal function tracking, or longer follow-up, the absence of reported adverse events does not establish a favorable safety profile. Hypercalcemia risk with high-dose vitamin D is well described in the literature and cannot be excluded here.
